LESSON: ACTIVE LISTENING, ORAL EXPRESSIONS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.5: Active Listening, Oral Expressions

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Active Listening, Oral Expressions. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we show that we are listening?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify listening markers in a text for communication
2. use acquired vocabulary to communicate in varied contexts
3. appreciate the role of vocabulary in foreign language learning

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ACTIVE LISTENING, ORAL EXPRESSIONS
Subject: GERMAN · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Active Listening, Oral Expressions helps you succeed in GERMAN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: ACTIVE LISTENING, ORAL EXPRESSIONS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify listening markers in a text for communication

What this means
In this part you learn to identify listening markers in a text for communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify listening markers in a text for communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Active Listening, Oral Expressions”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify listening markers in a text for communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use acquired vocabulary to communicate in varied contexts

What this means
In this part you learn to use acquired vocabulary to communicate in varied contexts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use acquired vocabulary to communicate in varied contexts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Active Listening, Oral Expressions to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use acquired vocabulary to communicate in varied contexts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of vocabulary in foreign language learning

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of vocabulary in foreign language learning. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of vocabulary in foreign language learning.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of vocabulary in foreign language learning. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Active Listening, Oral Expressions is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Active Listening, Oral Expressions”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify listening markers in a text for communication)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Active Listening, Oral Expressions to a partner. (skill: use acquired vocabulary to communicate in varied contexts)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of vocabulary in foreign language learning)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Active Listening, Oral Expressions to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify listening markers in a text for communication.
3. Practise this skill: use acquired vocabulary to communicate in varied contexts.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of vocabulary in foreign language learning.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Active Listening, Oral Expressions from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Active Listening, Oral Expressions: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Active Listening, Oral Expressions?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we show that we are listening?
2. How do we acquire vocabulary in a foreign language?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Active Listening, Oral Expressions means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify listening markers in a text for communication.
5. Be able to: use acquired vocabulary to communicate in varied contexts.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
